what_happened: The job "Make planner and critic derive history rules from every commit shape" (prompts) was rejected. The verdict was "fail: check test failed". One check failed: the test check. This is a check, not an acceptance criterion, and the event lists no unmet criteria and no blocker or major findings. The kept output for the check is only CI cleanup lines (git config includeIf removal, orphan process cleanup, a Node.js 20 deprecation warning). No test name or assertion is visible. So nobody can tell which test failed or why. The likely suspects are the prompt budget tests, since the job lengthened planner and critic prompts, but that is a guess.
cause: Athena stores the tail of the CI log as check output, and that tail is post-job cleanup. The failing test's name and assertion are cut off before they reach the record. Nothing extracts the failing test lines from the log or keeps them. So the verifier, the producer and the person running Athena cannot diagnose a test failure, and a retry cannot target it. The same truncation hit the previous job (20261106-045349-f6x6), and no fix for it has landed. Prompt edits also often break budget tests, but that cannot be confirmed here, because the evidence is lost.
prevention: When a test check fails, Athena should extract the failing test names, assertion messages and the cargo test summary from the full CI log (for example the "failures:" section and "test result:" lines) and store them as the check output, ahead of any cleanup tail. If extraction finds nothing, the record should say so explicitly. The check should also be rerun to separate a real failure from noise. Then every test failure leaves a readable cause for the producer, verifier and person running Athena.
proposed_request: Make the kept output of a failed test check show the cause of the failure. Today the record keeps only the tail of the CI log, which is post-job cleanup lines and warnings, so the failing test's name and assertion are lost (seen in jobs 20261106-045349-f6x6 and 20261027-054225-ycks). Outcome: when the test check fails, the stored check output contains the names of the failing tests, their assertion or panic messages, and the final "test result" summary, taken from the full log. If the log has none of these, the output says so in plain words. Cleanup and deprecation lines are dropped or placed after the failure details. Acceptance: (1) a test feeds a realistic CI log with one failing test followed by cleanup lines and shows the stored output names that test and its assertion; (2) a log with a failing budget test shows the budget test name; (3) a log with no recognisable failure lines gives the explicit "no failure lines found" message; (4) a passing log is unchanged; (5) cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy and cargo test pass. After it lands, re-ask job 20261027-054225-ycks (planner and critic derive history rules from every commit shape).
